function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve weather data from the Open-Meteo API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request. Each key-value pair represents a header field and its value.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters for the GET request.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location, positive for N and negative for S. This is a float type value.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location, positive for E and negative for W. This is a float type value.

elevation.description: Elevation in meters above sea level for the location. The default value represents no elevation downscaling.

auth.description: Authentication tuple for HTTP authentication, in the format (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem). A null value means no client certificate is used.

cookies.description: Dictionary of cookies to send with the request. Each key represents a cookie name.

proxies.description: Dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy. Each key-value pair represents a protocol and its proxy URL.

stream.description: If True, the response should be streamed; otherwise, it should be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate.

message.content:
Java is a high‑level, class‑based, object‑oriented programming language that was originally developed by James Gosling at Sun Microsystems (now owned by Oracle Corporation) and released in 1995. It’s designed to have as few implementation dependencies as possible, which is why it’s often described as “write once, run anywhere” (WORA). Here are some key points about Java:

| Feature | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| **Platform‑independent** | Java programs compile to bytecode, which runs on the Java Virtual Machine (JVM). The same bytecode can run on any device that has a JVM implementation. |
| **Object‑oriented** | Everything in Java is an object (except primitive types), making it easier to model real‑world entities and reuse code. |
| **Strongly typed** | Variables must be declared with a type, and type checking happens at compile time, reducing runtime errors. |
| **Automatic memory management** | Java uses garbage collection to automatically reclaim memory that is no longer referenced. |
| **Rich standard library** | The Java Standard Edition (SE) includes libraries for networking, I/O, collections, concurrency, GUI (Swing, JavaFX), and more. |
| **Multithreading support** | Java provides built‑in support for concurrent programming via threads and higher‑level concurrency utilities. |
| **Security features** | The JVM sandbox, bytecode verification, and security manager help protect against malicious code. |
| **Enterprise ecosystem** | Java Enterprise Edition (EE) adds APIs for web services, servlets, JavaServer Pages (JSP), Enterprise JavaBeans (EJB), and more. |
| **Community & tooling** | Popular IDEs include IntelliJ IDEA, Eclipse, and NetBeans. Build tools like Maven and Gradle manage dependencies and build processes. |

### Typical Use Cases

- **Web applications** – Servlets, JSP, Spring MVC, Jakarta EE.
- **Enterprise software** – Backend services, microservices, batch processing.
- **Mobile apps** – Android development (though Kotlin is now preferred, Java remains widely used).
- **Desktop applications** – Swing, JavaFX, or even simple console apps.
- **Embedded systems** – Java ME (Micro Edition) for devices with limited resources.
- **Big data & analytics** – Hadoop, Apache Spark (written in Scala but interoperable with Java).

### Why It Still Matters

Despite newer languages like Kotlin, Swift, or Rust, Java remains one of the most widely used languages worldwide. Its vast ecosystem, mature tooling, and strong backward compatibility make it a staple in many organizations’ technology stacks.

If you’re just starting out, learning Java gives you a solid foundation in object‑oriented concepts and a language that’s still in demand across many industries.
